clusterThemes: grant compliance checklists and prior approvals

queue.title: Post-Award Grant Management Checklist for Nonprofits
queue.brief: The checklist itself first (grouped: award acceptance, calendar and owners, restricted budget setup, evidence system, reporting cadence, prior approvals, closeout, retention), each item with the reason it exists and the primary source. Then how to run it monthly. Cite 2 CFR 200.328, 200.329, 200.308, 200.334, 200.344, 200.501 and Grants.gov post-award phase, with check dates. Federal vs foundation branches. Where software helps, using verified mechanics only.

queue.title: Grant Reporting Calendar Template for Nonprofits (Sheets, Excel, CSV)
queue.brief: Build a real CSV template (columns: funder, grant, award period, report type, due date, owner, evidence required, submitted date, status, notes) and save it under server/public/templates/grant-reporting-calendar-template.csv; link it for download and explain how to open it in Google Sheets and Excel. Explain how to fill it, monthly review rhythm, and the failure modes of a static sheet (no owner alerts, no evidence link, no burn view). Then how GrantConsole covers those gaps (verified facts only). FAQ on frequency of federal reports (200.328/200.329).

queue.title: Grant Closeout Checklist: Federal and Private Grants
queue.brief: Direct answer, then two branches: federal (120 calendar days for recipients, 90 for subrecipients per 200.344; final financial/performance reports per 200.328/200.329; liquidation; refunds; equipment/property; record retention 200.334) and private/foundation (award letter controls; typical final narrative + financial report; unspent funds; renewal conversation). Common closeout mistakes. Evidence and records to keep. Link the post-award checklist and the reporting calendar template.

queue.title: Restricted Funds Management for Nonprofits: Track Budget Burn by Grant Period
queue.brief: Restricted vs unrestricted in one paragraph (FASB ASC 958 terminology: net assets with donor restrictions — cite an authoritative explainer). Why calendar-based budget views mislead; the elapsed-period method with a worked example (e.g. $120,000 grant, 12-month period, month 5: 41.7% elapsed vs 58% spent = 16 points ahead). Warning signs, what to do when ahead/behind, allowability reminders (200.403). How GrantConsole computes burn against elapsed period and flags ±15 points (verified). Not accounting advice; does not replace fund accounting/GL.

queue.title: Grant Tracking Software for Nonprofits: Deadlines, Budgets, Evidence
queue.brief: Top-level product page. Direct answer: what grant tracking software should do for a recipient team. What nonprofit teams need to track (deadlines, owners, tasks, renewals, evidence, restricted budgets, risk). How GrantConsole does it — verified mechanics only, read shared/analytics.ts and server/services for accuracy. Spreadsheet vs software comparison table (honest: spreadsheets are fine below ~5 grants). Limitations (not discovery, not CRM, not accounting). FAQ. CTA demo. Use category 'product' (no external source required, but cite the eCFR when mentioning federal deadlines).

queue.title: Grant Reporting Software for Nonprofits: From Evidence to Funder Reports
queue.brief: Top-level product page. What belongs in a funder report (financial vs performance; 200.328/200.329 for federal), how evidence tied to deliverables removes the scramble, what a reporting packet contains in GrantConsole (verify in server/services/reports.ts and the packet page), activity history for reviewers. Limitations. FAQ. CTA demo.

queue.title: Grant Compliance Software for Grant Recipients: Explainable Rules and Activity History
queue.brief: Top-level product page. What 'compliance' means post-award for a recipient (scope: obligations in the award; not legal advice). Why explainable rules beat opaque health scores; the publicly documented rules with thresholds (verified list in CONTENT_GUIDE §3). Evidence and activity history. Explicit limitations: GrantConsole tracks what you enter; it does not interpret awards or make you compliant. Federal suitability framed carefully. FAQ. CTA demo.

queue.title: How to Track Multiple Grant Reporting Deadlines Without Spreadsheets
queue.brief: The failure pattern (deadlines in inboxes, one person's memory). A method: single source of truth, one owner per obligation, lead-time buffers, evidence readiness check at T-14, weekly 15-minute review. Options: shared calendar, project tool, template, dedicated software — honest pros/cons table. Where GrantConsole fits (verified). Link template and tracking page.

queue.title: How to Build an Audit-Ready Grant File (What to Keep and How to Organize It)
queue.brief: What an auditor or funder actually asks for; folder structure per grant (award documents, budget and revisions, approvals, expenditure support, deliverable evidence, reports submitted, correspondence, closeout); naming conventions; retention (200.334, three years from final financial report, exceptions); single audit threshold ($1,000,000, 200.501 — verify current). Evidence-to-deliverable linking as practice, then as product feature (verified).

queue.title: Restricted vs. Unrestricted Funds: What Nonprofit Grant Teams Need to Know
queue.brief: Plain-language definitions grounded in FASB ASC 958 (net assets with/without donor restrictions) citing an authoritative source; purpose vs time restrictions; how restrictions are released; how grants create restrictions; operational consequences for tracking (per-grant budgets, burn against period). Common mistakes. Not accounting advice; talk to your auditor.

queue.title: Grant Administration vs. Grant Management: What's the Difference?
queue.brief: Clarify overlapping terms: pre-award vs post-award; grantee vs grantmaker perspective; roles (grants manager, grant administrator, program officer). Table of who does what. Where software categories map (discovery, application, grantmaker GMS, recipient post-award). Position GrantConsole in the recipient post-award cell only.

queue.title: What Is Grant Management Software? A Guide for Grant Recipients
queue.brief: Category definition with the crucial split: grantmaker systems vs recipient tools vs discovery databases. What recipient-side software should do (deadlines, budgets, evidence, reporting, roles, audit trail). What to look for (checklist of buying criteria). When a spreadsheet is enough. GrantConsole as one example in the recipient post-award category (verified).

queue.title: Grant Budget Burn Rate: How to Tell When a Grant Is Spending Too Fast or Too Slow
queue.brief: Formula (spent % minus elapsed %), tolerance bands, two worked examples, why straight-line isn't always right (seasonal programs, front-loaded equipment), what to do (rebudget within rules; prior approval thresholds 200.308; no-cost extension basics), when underspending leads to returned funds. GrantConsole's ±15-point rule (verified).

queue.title: Funder Report Preparation Checklist: What to Gather Before You Write
queue.brief: T-30/T-14/T-7/T-1 checklist; content of performance reports per 200.329 (comparison of accomplishments to objectives, reasons for slippage, cost overruns) and financial reports per 200.328; foundation report norms; evidence list; internal review and sign-off; submission proof and filing. Link reporting software page and calendar template.

queue.title: Grant Management Software Comparison for Recipients: Criteria, Sources, Dates
keywords: best grant management software for nonprofits
queue.brief: Methodology first (criteria, how facts were gathered, check dates, corrections policy). Include only products whose current positioning, audience and features can be verified from their own public pages fetched during the run (candidates: Instrumentl, Foundant GrantHub, Fluxx Grantseeker, AmpliFund, GrantPipe, ActivityInfo, Submittable — verify each and drop any you cannot). Recipient-side vs grantmaker vs discovery classification. Neutral 'who should look elsewhere' for every tool including GrantConsole. No scores, no invented pricing; link to each vendor's pricing page. Update log section.

queue.title: How Development and Finance Teams Share Responsibility for Active Grants
queue.brief: RACI-style table for post-award tasks (calendar, budgets, expenditures, evidence, reports, prior approvals, closeout, audit); the handoffs that fail; a monthly grants-finance meeting agenda; role-based access as a practice and (verified) as a product feature. Link tracking page.

queue.title: Federal Grant Prior Approval Requirements (2 CFR 200.308): What Needs Sign-Off
queue.brief: List each item in 200.308(f) verbatim-adjacent with plain explanations; the one-time no-cost extension (up to 12 months, written notice at least 10 calendar days before the period ends); how to document requests and approvals in the grant file. Verify every clause on eCFR the day of writing. Not legal advice. Link audit-ready file and closeout checklist.

queue.title: Grant Record Retention Requirements: How Long to Keep Grant Files
keywords: how long to keep grant records
queue.brief: Three years from the final financial report (200.334) and each exception (litigation/audit findings, property records three years after disposition, program income, indirect cost proposals, agency written notice); private funder norms; a simple retention schedule table; where records live and how to prove completeness. Link audit-ready file.

queue.title: Moving From Spreadsheets to Grant Management Software: A Migration Plan
keywords: when to stop using spreadsheets for grants
queue.brief: Signals you have outgrown the sheet; what to inventory before moving (grants, funders, periods, budgets, deliverables, evidence locations, owners); a two-week migration plan; data-hygiene rules; how to run both in parallel for one cycle; what a spreadsheet still does well. Demo as a way to test the fit (verified).

queue.title: Grant Renewal Planning Checklist: Start 90 Days Before the Period Ends
queue.brief: T-90/T-60/T-30 checklist; evidence of results to assemble; conversation with the program officer; budget lessons from burn data; decision to renew or exit; how a renewal deliverable keeps this visible (verified: GrantConsole flags renewal windows within 90 days with no renewal deliverable scheduled).

queue.title: Subrecipient Monitoring Checklist for Pass-Through Nonprofits
queue.brief: For nonprofits that pass federal funds to partners: subrecipient vs contractor determination (200.331), required subaward information and risk assessment (200.332), monitoring activities, subrecipient deadlines (90 days for final reports per 200.344), documentation. Verify every clause on eCFR the day of writing. Not legal advice.

queue.title: Are We on Top of Our Grants? Questions Boards and Executive Directors Should Ask
queue.brief: Ten questions with the evidence that answers each (awarded value, reports due next 90 days and readiness, burn variance outliers, evidence gaps, unowned grants, renewals in window, closeouts pending); a one-page monthly grants dashboard outline; how explainable warnings help leadership trust the answer (verified).

queue.title: Tying Evidence to Deliverables: A Simple System for Grant Documentation
queue.brief: Map every deliverable to the evidence that proves it before work starts; naming, storage, required-count checks; the T-14 evidence readiness check; examples across program types; how this shortens reporting and audits. Product tie-in verified (evidence attached to the deliverable that requires it; evidence-gap rules).

queue.title: Grant Management Software Pricing: Models to Expect and Questions to Ask
queue.brief: Category-level only: common models (per user, per grant/award volume, tiers, implementation fees, annual contracts, nonprofit discounts) with links to vendors' public pricing pages fetched during the run and check dates; total-cost questions to ask; how to size for 5–30 grants. Do not state or imply any GrantConsole price; say pricing questions go to /contact.

queue.title: Grant Management KPIs for Nonprofits: Reporting Readiness, Burn Variance and More
queue.brief: Eight metrics with definitions, formulas, and healthy ranges framed as practice not benchmark data (on-time report rate, evidence readiness at T-14, burn variance, unowned obligations, closeout on time, renewal coverage, prior-approval turnaround, audit findings); a monthly review template.

queue.title: Underspent Grant? What to Do Before the Period Ends
queue.brief: Diagnose the cause, options in order (accelerate allowable work, rebudget within rules, request approval, no-cost extension per 200.308, plan for return), how to talk to the funder early, documentation. Foundation vs federal differences. Verified product tie-in for the behind-schedule rule.

queue.title: Grant Spending Ahead of Schedule: How to Course-Correct Before Funds Run Out
queue.brief: Distinguish front-loaded plans from real overruns; allowability and allocability reminders (200.403); options (slow discretionary spend, reallocate within approvals, seek supplemental funds, adjust scope with approval); communicating with the funder; documentation. Verified tie-in for the ahead-of-schedule rule.

queue.title: How to Request a No-Cost Extension on a Grant (Federal and Foundation)
queue.brief: When an extension is appropriate and when it is not (not merely to spend down); federal one-time extension rules and notice timing (verify 200.308(g)); what to include in the request; foundation practice; how to reflect the new end date in your calendar and burn calculations. Not legal advice.

queue.title: Grant Management for Small Nonprofits: A Lean System for 5–25 Grants
queue.brief: A minimum viable post-award system for a one- or two-person team: intake, calendar, budgets, evidence, monthly review, reporting, closeout; time budget per week; when to move from spreadsheet to software. Pull the checklists together as a hub-like guide.

queue.title: Post-Award Grant Management Glossary: 40 Terms Explained
queue.brief: Forty terms with one-paragraph definitions in plain language, each linking to the resource that covers it in depth; federal terms cite the eCFR definitions section (200.1) where applicable. Alphabetical; add anchor-friendly headings.
